newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil rise on crude rally.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil rise on crude rally.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and naphtha swaps rose at midday on Wednesday on a hefty 57-cent gain to overnight crude rally, traders said.
"Gas oil firmed this morning because of the big increase in overnight crude prices," one trader said.
August swaps were indicated at $21.60/$21.75 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $21.20/$21.30. August traded in the morning at $21.70 and $21.75 before easing slightly to trade at $21.65, brokers said.
July also chalked up impressive gains with the July/August spread at a traded narrow level of minus 55 cents compared to Monday's minus 75 cents.
July was last quoted at $21.00/$21.20, compared to Monday's $20.50/$20.60, brokers said. It traded earlier in the day at $21.20, they said.
The August/September contango remains wide but is coming in slightly with a trade done earlier in the day at minus 80 cents, from Tuesday's trade of minus 85 cents, brokers said.
Overnight August Brent crude closed up 57 cents to $18.41 per barrel, on bullish American Petroleum Institute (API) stocks data.
Traders said the gas oil market fundamentals were unchanged with supply seen in excess of demand.
Physical sellers were expected to maintain their aggressive offers in an effort to get rid of prompt barrels.
On Tuesday cargoes were offered down to a low of $20.50 per barrel but no buyers emerged.
Fuel oil swaps were steady with August and September last quoted unchanged at $98.00/$99.00.
Naphtha swaps rose sharply in tandem with the stronger crude and a prompt physical squeeze.
August was last quoted at $21.65/$21.80 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $21.30 traded level.
